quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel back the other way.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Rely only on your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Place your right arm on the back of the passenger seat and look directly through the rear window. Do not use only your mirrors, as they cannot show what is directly behind your vehicle. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: You are on the freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.
Always maintain your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic, if possible.
questions.explanation: When traffic permits, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signals when parking next to a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
When pulling next to, but not away from, the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Signal when pulling next to a curb and when pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The lane to the right may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is prohibited from both directions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, park within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: Is it ever unsafe to drive 10 mph if it is the posted speed limit?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Drive slower than the posted speed limit when conditions require it. Bad traffic, weather, or visibility may require you to drive as slowly as 10 miles per hour.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks entering.
Truck exit only.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep downgrade is ahead. Check your brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a larger distance between your vehicle and the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three to four seconds of distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely, you and the rider are in danger. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. Wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges increase the chance of a fall.

questions.question: If a school bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway, must you stop?

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus with its lights on and stop arm out. However, you do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off water droplets and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
After you signal for three seconds.
When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Make sure you are far enough ahead of the vehicle you passed before moving back into your lane. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, yield to any driver who:

options.text: Is on your left.
Arrived at the intersection before you did.
Is across from your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrived at the intersection before you did.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go through in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the one on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-lane road unless:

options.text: You can see the road clearly ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle has enough power to pass.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You need all three conditions to pass safely on a two-lane road: clear visibility ahead, room to return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and a vehicle that can reach the right speed to pass. Only pass where it is legal and safe.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if there is also a green circular light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go, just like a green circle. But you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: A steady red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.

questions.question: When passing on a highway with multiple lanes:

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before you pass, check that the passing lane is clear and use your turn signal to show you are changing lanes.

questions.question: As you approach a roundabout, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Enter without yielding because you have the right-of-way.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Wait until all other traffic has left the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: Yield to all vehicles already in the roundabout. Traffic moves counterclockwise, so vehicles will approach from your left.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit based on road conditions. However, you cannot drive faster than the posted limit. You must slow down for curves, hills with poor visibility, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: Using a cell phone to talk or text while driving does not increase your risk of a crash.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving is a distraction. It increases your risk of being in a crash.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes, turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabled permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and at least one passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces reserved for people with disabled permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled permits.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You may proceed in the direction of a green arrow if you are in the correct lane, regardless of other signals. Before turning, you must let pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection go first.
